solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pictures an iPhone is apt to take?

definitions.text: Pictures an iPhone is apt to take?

parts.words: Pictures an iPhone is apt to take?
parts.note: the 'i' of iPhone is read as the self, so the phone's natural photos are of its owner

explanation.surface: A remark about the kind of photos a smartphone tends to produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'i' in iPhone puns on 'I', the person holding it: what such a phone takes is pictures of oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-portrait photos taken at arm's length on a phone are the typical smartphone snapshots.

clue.text: Boy seen around little devils in Homer?

indicators.note: seen around means placed round, so the boy word encloses the devils

parts.note: a boy is a son
imps are little devils

explanation.surface: A lad surrounded by mischief-makers in the Greek poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the ancient poet, but it is Homer Simpson of the TV cartoon, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the father in the cartoon The Simpsons, so Homer is one example of a Simpson.

clue.text: A labourer that loan gets on top of gets help

indicators.note: in a down clue being on top of means coming before, so the loan word goes first

parts.note: to lend is to loan
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A worker burdened by a debt ends up getting some assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is the idiom for assisting someone.

clue.text: Love kept one up in a state

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
had means kept, as in had it in stock
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Affection that kept someone's spirits high, in a fretful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: O + HAD + I reads OHADI, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west.

clue.text: Drunk Iranians will hug democratic European

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the reworked letters wrap round the other piece
drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat or democratic

explanation.surface: Tipsy Iranians embrace a European with democratic leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges IRANIANS to SAR-INIAN, which 'will hug' wraps round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is an Italian island, so a Sardinian is a European.

clue.text: Warning: contrary setter's a bit of a beast

parts.note: 'Fore!' is the golfer's shouted warning

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the setter word is read backwards

parts.note: gel is something that sets, a setting agent; the 's links

explanation.surface: A cautionary note that the puzzle's compiler is a bit beastly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is GEL, a substance that sets, which 'contrary' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A front leg is one part of an animal's body, so it is a bit of a beast.

clue.text: Cast with bit of finesse to get fish

indicators.note: a bit of the word here is its opening letter

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler casts with some skill to land a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like an angler's action next to 'fish', but it is the definition, meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is to throw it hard, a synonym of cast.

clue.text: Army groups miner gets to redeploy

indicators.note: redeploying moves units into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military units that a mine worker is set to reposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to redeploy' rearranges MINER GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent unit of an army, so regiments are military groupings.

clue.text: Prayer service peers heard on the radio

indicators.note: what is heard on the radio is only spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: lords are peers, members of the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords broadcast during a morning act of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LORDS and LAUDS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauds is the morning office of prayer in the Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Pineapple mostly found on American island

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: pineapple is old military slang for a hand grenade, from its shape

explanation.surface: Most of a tropical fruit turns up on an island in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims GRENADE to GRENAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Chap with short joke is a foreign comic

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the joke word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A fellow with a brief quip turns out to be a comedian from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims GAG to GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Manga are Japanese comic books, so one is a comic from overseas.

clue.text: Instrument used to measure cats and dogs?

definitions.text: Instrument used to measure cats and dogs?

parts.words: Instrument used to measure cats and dogs?
parts.note: 'raining cats and dogs' means pouring with rain, so the device measuring it measures rainfall

explanation.surface: An absurd device for sizing up household pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'raining cats and dogs' means heavy rain, so measuring 'cats and dogs' means measuring rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge collects and records how much precipitation falls, the downpour of the idiom.

clue.text: Salt perhaps hot to break into shanty?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes into the song

parts.note: a shanty is a sea song, sung by sailors
hot means fashionable, which is IN

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some salt-loving sailor might burst into a work song.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes inside SEA SONG after its N, giving SEASON-IN-G. 'Salt' looks like a sailor beside 'shanty', but it is the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is one example of a flavouring added to food, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Former F1 driver spotted in Bahamas sailing

indicators.note: spotted in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired racing driver has been seen yachting in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Felipe Massa is a Brazilian who raced for Ferrari and Williams in Formula One until 2017.

clue.text: Lugs getting behind new approaches

indicators.note: getting behind puts the lugs word after the other piece

parts.note: lugs is slang for ears

explanation.surface: Some ears stand behind something new as it draws closer.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come closer to it, so nears and approaches are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Broken Easter egg must be set apart

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cracked chocolate egg must be kept away from the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges EASTER EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate or isolate, keeping one group apart from another.

clue.text: Insane do I crashed in the country

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they lost their mind and crashed while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges INSANE DO I.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Insult series of lectures in communication

parts.note: to dis is slang for to insult
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Rude remarks made in a lecture series about how people communicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is spoken or written exchange of ideas, a form of communication.

clue.text: Cloak acquired by southern lech for Patsy

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in by, so the cloak goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a goat is slang for a lecherous man
a cape is a cloak

explanation.surface: A lecher from the south gets a cloak meant for a woman named Patsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patsy' looks like a woman's name, but it means someone who takes the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is someone made to carry the blame for others, a fall guy.

clue.text: Poor folk surrounded by DI's men

parts.note: something surrounded by others is in them, giving IN
DI is a Detective Inspector, taken as written; the 's joins him to his men
gents are men

explanation.surface: Destitute people find themselves encircled by a detective's officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy or impoverished, so indigents are the destitute.

clue.text: Fancy old lady opening one spirit with energy

indicators.note: opening means prising apart, so the old lady goes into the gap

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit
ma is a familiar name for one's mother, the old lady
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An elderly woman cracks open some gin with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to suppose or picture it in the mind, as imagine does.

clue.text: Small instrument tuned a little high?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A little musical instrument whose pitch is set slightly too high.
explanation.definitionFit: A note played or sung sharp is pitched slightly above where it should be.

clue.text: Member seen with leader is an idiot

parts.note: pin is slang for a leg, a limb or member
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A club member spotted with the boss turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhead is a stupid person, as though their head were as small as a pin's.

clue.text: A large individual with no friends?

parts.note: an individual is one

explanation.surface: A big person without any companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without friends or company is on their own, solitary.

clue.text: Done with time in the public eye?

parts.note: something done is over, finished

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone's spell of fame has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden from view.

clue.text: Vegetable abroad Ben served in a new way

indicators.note: dishing something up in a new way rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's item that Ben, overseas, had prepared differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in a new way' rearranges ABROAD BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad bean is a large flat bean eaten as a green vegetable.

clue.text: Sign Harry will split from foremost of royals

indicators.note: splitting from something means leaving it, so that letter drops out

parts.note: to badger is to harry, pester

indicators.note: foremost of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A hint that Prince Harry will break away from the leading royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince, but it is a verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or token worn to show membership, a sign.

clue.text: Duke associated with playboy explorer

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: An aristocrat linked with a womanising adventurer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who sailed round the world.

clue.text: Calender I repaired for a foreign national

indicators.note: repaired means fixed and put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fixed a pressing machine for a visitor from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges CALENDER I; a calender is a machine that presses cloth or paper between rollers.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Iceland is a national of a country other than Britain.

clue.text: Love men found in Aden briefly

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
briefly means cut short, so the port's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen, taken as written
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms among soldiers stationed in the Yemeni port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ADEN to ADE and 'found in' sets the soldiers inside; 'men' as OR (other ranks) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to be devoted to them, a strong form of loving.

clue.text: Old engineers restricting temperature limit

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the outer pieces close round the other

parts.note: ex means former, old
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Veteran engineers keep a lid on the heat at its maximum.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the outermost point or furthest degree of something, a limit.

clue.text: Chosen to get rid of section in office?

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so the section letter is dropped

parts.note: selected means chosen

explanation.surface: Picked to clear out a department at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chosen' looks like the definition, but it is SELECTED losing S; the definition is the question at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who has been voted in holds office, so is in office.
